t: A German-speaking merchant town under Lübeck law, granted self-government by King Eric IV of Denmark in 1248.
It prospered as a Hanseatic link between Novgorod and Lübeck, governed by a council drawn from the Great Guild.
Ruled by Denmark and from 1346 by the Teutonic Order, it submitted to Sweden in 1561 during the Livonian War.
dyk: Reval's Brotherhood of the Blackheads, an association of unmarried merchants, took its name from its patron Saint Maurice, shown as a Moor on its coat of arms.
ev: Valdemar II defeats the Estonians at Lindanise and builds a castle on Toompea
Eric IV of Denmark grants the town Lübeck law
Estonian rebels besiege Reval in the St George's Night Uprising
Denmark sells northern Estonia, with Reval, to the Teutonic Order
The Gothic town hall is completed
Iconoclastic riots mark the Lutheran Reformation in Reval
Reval submits to Eric XIV of Sweden during the Livonian War

f.founder: Eric IV of Denmark (grant of Lübeck law)
